This is an edit. When I finished the charts, I had family commitments and couldnt provide a commentary; apologies.

The main focus of this analysis is on identifying where the key zones are in the PA. have been studying a lot of the journals here and pulling it together as best I can.

There are essentially 3 zones here, delineated by the zone in the middle. I have picked up the FTR on the left at the top as being a place where a pause occurs at the edge of a PAZ. An engulf had already taken place and price had capped nicely, and the CP back up to the edge of the zone was a confluence indicator that price might be headed south when it eventually reaches the opposite end of this upper zone. Price moves between the opposite ends of the zones, and then decisions are made. The pause at the top demarks the a decision - price stalled, brielfy, and it could have gone north and returned into the zone and would have been an FO. But it doesnt. Its form manifests as price drops south and this becomes our FTR.

Down in the middle, we have a flag limit and I also pick this up as an FTR. Price hhas halted here, and very well could have reversed back up. But it doesnt. It bases, and then its form again is made manifest, and it is decided it is still too expensive, in the middle of the value curve here. So this is another FTR.

Down at the bottom I marked out what I see as being a key area of price action, and there is a nice FO DBR out and back in from underneath. This movement causes a nice RBR which engulfs the recent high. And in fact the box here could have started higher. After the engulf, one sign prices might be headed higher, the pullback comes back into the zone and bounces of a support level. This itself engulfs the last high that was formed (not shown), but the engulf had already happened, and readying to take a position had already ensued.

Naturally, price makes its way to the opposite end of the zone (flag) and bounces back in from the FL. A few attempts are made, and indeed there are a few short trades here that I havent shown to avoid over cluttering the chart. The nice thing about all of this is that price comes back to where it wants to be - the origin. Within this area an engulf north happens (on the right at the bottom of the chart), and price bounces (naturally) back down from the FL. We have a double bottom and double top. Notice also just to the left, price makes a little CP as it rises, before price plummets. This is a nice movement for the pro money because it allows them to take the liquidity on the way down so that they can load up for the big move up to the top zone that they are look to. So price bounces from that small FL and makes its way back down to the demand zone that was created by the FTR all the way on the left. This double bottom is capped, and for sure this was a place to take an aggressive long position. From here price engulfs the latest high before retreating slightly (FTR). This base at the edge of the zone causes a new makjor move up. Also notice on right at the top edge of the magenta rectangle, a little blip that I point to indicating an FTR. At the edge of this zone, a stall unfolds, but it is decided it is too cheap, and price rises strongly. Nicely, price makes its way all the way to the top, to the FTR that caused the move down right at the left of the chart. A nice TT trade or such like down from this FTB to the FTR could have been taken.

When price falls under the supply at the FTR, where is its target? The FTR that caused the move up - that tiny blip/FL/FTR at the edge of the flag down at the bottom. See the second chart - it shows what happens when price returns to the source.

Hopefully this explains my thinking clearly.

Metta,

hey all.

working on spotting fake outs at the moment.

i have AUDUSD 4H with explanation, i think i got it right in regard to finding and understanding the dynamics of a fake out to some degree. obviously there are different kinds of fake outs to take into account.

#1 was a previous swing high with DP to take price lower and then a retest with in a short while before taking it lower again.

#2 was another level looks like a flag/DP where most markets participants where waiting to take price lower it retested it 2-3 times. from what i understand, everyone is selling at this level so in order for the pro money to get in, they will look for liquidity. the big blue candle breaking higher @3 is where all the sell stops are triggered and buyers entering while pro taking the other side.

#4 price revisits the previous swing high this is where money are turning price and as price starts moving down all the buy stops are triggered and more sellers getting in thus causing price to shoot down with mom.

this is one example of a fake to my understanding. all i have to say is the pro money are smart but im studying them:D

PS. i also remember reading somewhere that an engulf can mean one of two things. 1. price is in fact heading higher with strong momentum to take price to a new low/high or 2. price is making a strong mom candle to catch everyone getting in that candle before price reversing. thus a fake out candle
